title: Tenant-driven retry amplification: implement dedupe lease + per-tenant circuit shim to stop 5xx cascades
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sustained spikes of 5xx and high tail latency during tenant bursts. Root-cause analysis shows retry amplification originating from edge proxy replays + client SDK retries for non-idempotent routes. Amplified traffic overloaded the model-serving queues and caused KV-cache churn and queue stalls, producing cascading 5xx responses and long recoveries. This ticket scopes a short-term hotfix (dedupe lease + emergency tenant circuit) and a medium-term follow-up (SDK backoff alignment, proxy replay rules, telemetry per-tenant).
steps_taken: 2025-02-15: Pager triaged by SRE. Initial mitigation: increase worker pool slightly and temporarily tighten circuit-breaker thresholds (manual).

2025-02-16: Captured trace samples from affected tenants; identified duplicate payloads with identical request fingerprints replayed within 600ms window (edge replay + SDK retry). Linked traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/hosted-api-traces?var-tenant=tenant-42

2025-02-17: Hotfix proposal: implement short-lived server-side 'dedupe lease' keyed by tenant+payload-hash with TTL 1s and early-fastfail if lease in-flight >3x threshold. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12877
2025-02-18: Conducted load test with synthetic tenant bursts (k=10k reqs/s) in staging; dedupe lease reduced model invocation duplicates by 86% and reduced 95th latency by 42% in the scenario.

2025-02-19: Deployed rolling canary to 10% of hosts in us-west and enabled tenant admission cap for the top 5 tenants. Observed drop in 5xx rates for canary tenants. Metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/tenant-throttle-overview

2025-02-21: Deployed emergency tenant-level circuit shim that opens at sustained queueing >200ms and inflight >1200 for a tenant; fallback policy returns explanatory 429 with diagnostic ID and triggers tenant notifications. Runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tenant+Throttling+Runbook
decision_log: Adopt dedupe-lease rather than global de-duplication to minimize cross-tenant state and keep low memory footprint.
Short TTL (1s) chosen because request replay window observed <600ms; conservative TTL avoids blocking legitimate retries across network spikes.
Implement tenant circuit shim as a soft-open 'shelving' state that returns 429 + diagnostic tag rather than 503 to preserve signal for SDKs and reduce retries.
Align SDK retry policy with platform: SDKs will be updated to default max_retries=2, exponential backoff with jitter, and honor X-Idempotency-Key if provided.
Proxy replay behavior: disable automatic idempotent-less replays for POST/text-generation routes; require explicit Idempotency header for replayable requests.
review_feedback: PM Priya Shah: requested per-tenant telemetry to be surfaced to account teams before wide rollout (action: add per-tenant error budget metric).
Design Liam O'Connor: asked to provide UX copy for 429 diagnostic page and suggested adding an explanation to the Dashboard tenant details view.
Security team: reviewed dedupe lease implementation for leakage risk; recommended scoped cache encryption and TTL enforcement (done).
next_steps: Merge and monitor hotfix PR #12877 and related runtime changes. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12877
Publish SDK patch aligning retry semantics and a migration guide for customers to opt into Idempotency headers.
Add per-tenant telemetry and alerting in Console: error-budget by tenant, inflight counts, dedupe-hit-rate.
Run a coordinated customer communication for affected tenants explaining 429 behavior and guidance to add idempotency keys for long-running operations.
Medium-term: replace ad-hoc leases with a sharded, low-latency dedupe store (runtime-1.21) and formalize proxy replay rules.
postmortem_notes: Root cause summary: combination of edge-proxy replay + client retries caused duplicate, tightly-timed requests to pile up and saturate downstream model queues. Our serving runtime lacked a cheap de-duplication/lease mechanism for recently-inflight requests and tenant-scoped admission controls were insufficient.
What worked: quick targeted canary, dedupe lease reduced duplicates quickly, tenant circuit shim prevented cascade recovery times.
What didn't: lack of per-tenant telemetry slowed initial threat assessment; SDKs did not expose idempotency guidance clearly.
Follow-ups assigned to Product and SDK teams to coordinate migration plan and docs.
notes: Coordinate customer comms with AE team; suggest offering a short-term Dedicated capacity allocation for customers that request isolation while we roll out long-term mitigations.
Estimate for full solution (sharded dedupe store + proxy ruleset + SDK rollout): ~3 sprints across runtime, proxy, and SDK teams.
Engineering rota: Jonah to lead hotfix until 2025-02-28, then handoff to infra-maintainers team.
